heading: INT. MOBILE CLINIC - CONVERTED BOOKMOBILE - DAY

units.text: INT. MOBILE CLINIC - CONVERTED BOOKMOBILE - DAY
A city bookmobile gutted and refitted.
Shelves that once held paperbacks now hold gauze and saline.
A folding exam bed.
A hand-lettered sign: CLOSE THE DOOR SOFTLY.
DR. HALVORSEN LUNDQVIST, fifties, tired, sits on a stool with a blood pressure cuff in her lap.
NURSE PIA OKONKWO, thirties, wipes down a tray.
ELIAS BRANDT, seventy, shirtless to the waist, sits on the exam bed.
His wife MRS. DOROTA BRANDT, also seventy, stands by the door with her purse held in front of her like a shield.
Elias grips the bed's edge.
Dr. Lundqvist and Pia look at the monitor at the same time.
Pia reaches for the cuff.
The doctor reaches for it too.
Their hands meet on it and they both stop.
Go ahead.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Pia wraps the cuff around Elias's arm.
Dorota takes a step in.
Elias lifts his free hand to stop her.
I'm fine.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: You're grey.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: It's the light in here.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: It's not the light, Mr. Brandt.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Pia pumps the bulb.
Everyone watches the needle fall.
One-sixty over ninety-eight.
units.name: PIA

units.text: That's better than it was twenty minutes ago.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: What was it twenty minutes ago?
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: One-ninety over a hundred and ten.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Dorota sits on the bench seat under the window.
She puts her purse on her knees and then, after a moment, on the floor.
He wouldn't come in. For three days, he wouldn't come in.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: I had the garden.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: You had a chest like a drum and you had the garden.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Dorota.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Don't Dorota me in front of the nurse.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: It's all right, Mrs. Brandt.
units.name: PIA

units.text: It isn't, though. I'm sorry. It isn't.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Mr. Brandt, how long have you had the pain in your left arm?
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Since Tuesday.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Since Sunday.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Since Sunday. Fine.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: And the shortness of breath?
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: When I climb the stairs.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: When he climbs anything.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: We're going to do an ECG. It's painless. Some stickers on your chest.
units.name: PIA

units.text: I know what an ECG is.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: I know you know.
units.name: PIA

units.text: Pia opens a drawer and peels three electrodes from a sheet.
Elias watches her hands.
My brother had one of those.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: What happened?
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: He's dead.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Elias.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: You asked.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: I did. I'm sorry for the loss. When was this?
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Nineteen ninety-one. Heart attack at fifty-four. He was cutting a hedge.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: That is useful for me to know. I'm going to write it down.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Dr. Lundqvist writes.
Pia presses the stickers to his chest, left, right, low.
Cold?
units.name: PIA

units.text: Everything's cold.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: The heater's broken. They said Thursday.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: They said Thursday last Thursday.
units.name: PIA

units.text: They did.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: A small laugh passes through the bookmobile, the first.
It dies quickly.
Okay. Lie back for me.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Elias lies back.
Pia clips the leads on.
The monitor draws a line, then another, then a rhythm.
Dr. Lundqvist and Pia both lean toward the screen.
They look at each other.
Neither speaks.
Dr. Lundqvist exhales through her nose.
No ST elevation.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: No.
units.name: PIA

units.text: That's good.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: What does that mean?
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: It means he is not having a heart attack right now. It does not mean he did not have a small one on Sunday.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Can you tell?
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: We can draw blood. It takes about an hour at the hospital.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: I'm not going to the hospital.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: You are going to the hospital.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Dorota.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: You are going to the hospital and I am going to sit in the plastic chair and hold your coat.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Who'll feed the cat?
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: The cat has eaten since nineteen eighty-eight without you.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: That's a lie. I fed it this morning.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: That is what I mean.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Elias laughs, once, and winces, and presses a hand flat to his sternum.
Stop laughing. Pia, aspirin, please. Chewed, not swallowed.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Right away.
units.name: PIA

units.text: And call the ambulance. Tell them stable, chest pain, seventy-year-old male.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Pia takes a phone from the shelf.
Dorota rises, goes to the bed, and puts her hand over her husband's hand on his chest.
He looks at the ceiling.
She looks at the monitor.
Mrs. Brandt, he'll be fine for the next little while. I'd like you to sit with him.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: I am sitting with him.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Yes. Thank you.
units.name: DR. LUNDQVIST

units.text: Hello? Yes. Mobile clinic on Ostrow Street, by the bakery.
units.name: PIA

units.text: Don't let them touch my garden tools.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Nobody wants your garden tools.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: The good trowel.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: I will guard the trowel with my life.
units.name: DOROTA

units.text: Pia hangs up and hands Elias an aspirin.
He puts it in his mouth and grimaces.
The monitor goes on drawing its line.
